name: Insurance
one_liner: Insurers pool risk by collecting premiums upfront and paying claims later, profiting from underwriting discipline and from investing the float in between.
how_it_makes_money: Property & casualty insurers aim for an underwriting profit (premiums above claims and expenses) plus investment income on the float. Life and annuity insurers earn the spread between investment returns and the rates credited to policyholders, plus fees on retirement products; brokers earn commissions without taking risk.
revenue_formula: Earned premiums = policies in force × average premium × retention
Underwriting profit = earned premiums × (1 - combined ratio)
cost_structure: Losses and loss adjustment expenses: claims paid and reserved, by far the largest cost
Acquisition costs: agent and broker commissions
Operating expenses: underwriting, policy administration, technology
Reinsurance premiums: ceded to transfer peak and catastrophe risk
Regulatory capital and compliance: state-by-state rules in the US
margins: A P&C combined ratio below 100% means underwriting profit, and most profit years land roughly in the 90s; returns on equity are often high single to low double digits, driven by pricing discipline, catastrophe exposure, and investment yields.

key_metrics.name: Combined ratio
key_metrics.what: Losses plus expenses divided by earned premium; below 100% signals an underwriting profit.

key_metrics.name: Loss ratio
key_metrics.what: Claims and adjustment costs over earned premium; the core test of pricing and risk selection.

key_metrics.name: Expense ratio
key_metrics.what: Acquisition and operating costs over premium; reflects distribution and operating efficiency.

key_metrics.name: Gross written premium (GWP)
key_metrics.what: Total premium written in a period; the top-line growth measure.

key_metrics.name: Retention / persistency
key_metrics.what: Share of policies that renew; drives lifetime value given high acquisition costs.

key_metrics.name: Investment yield
key_metrics.what: Return on the invested float; a major profit driver especially for life insurers.

key_metrics.name: Solvency / RBC ratio
key_metrics.what: Capital relative to required regulatory capital; indicates financial strength.

trends: Rising catastrophe losses from severe weather push up property rates and trigger market exits in high-risk states
Auto insurers repricing after a period of rising repair costs and claims severity
Higher interest rates boosting investment income and annuity sales
Private equity-backed firms acquiring life and annuity blocks
Telematics, AI underwriting and claims automation
Embedded insurance sold at the point of purchase
